thread:
incident-bot: Pager ALERT: HIGH - Dedicated pool 'pegasus-prod' p95 token latency > 1.5s for 12m. Affected tenant(s): PegasusCorp (enterprise VPC). Paging oncall: @oncall-sylvia. Alert: https://alerts.redwood/INC-1934567899 :rotating_light:

oncall-sylvia: On it. Joining bridge now. Any known deploys?

ops-jake: No deploys in the window. Seeing sustained tail queue growth on host gp3-peg-01..04. Noise seems correlated with large batch requests from PegasusCorp.

eng-runtime-chandra: Can you paste the tail logs for request batching? Also pinging runtime infra to check KV cache hit rates. Might be a routing imbalance.

compute-tilly: GPU utilization 92% across pool, but three hosts show memory spikes ~88% and OOM retransmits. Suspect shard hotspot.

oncall-sylvia: Quick mitigation: will remove PegasusCorp from shared burst lane and shift to reserved capacity lane, then evaluate. Executing isolation now.

oncall-sylvia: ```
# move tenant to isolated pool
redwoodctl tenant migrate --tenant PegasusCorp --from pegasus-prod --to pegasus-reserved-01
# adjust routing weight
redwoodctl route update --pool pegasus-prod --tenant PegasusCorp --weight 0
```

incident-bot: Action logged: tenant migration initiated by oncall-sylvia at 1934567975.

ops-jake: After migration, observed immediate drop in queuing on gp3-peg-02 and gp3-peg-03. p95 now ~420ms (was 1.7s). Good sign.

eng-runtime-chandra: Thanks. Still seeing KV cache cold misses for that tenant on the reserved pool — need a warm-up plan and a short kernel fallback patch to avoid repeated cold-start tails. Proposing a quick config change to increase in-memory cache window for 30m.

eng-runtime-chandra: ```
# temporary cache window bump
redwoodctl config set --pool pegasus-reserved-01 --kv_cache_window 30m
```

compute-tilly: Applied cache window bump. GPU memory pressure stabilized. Latency trending to normal.

incident-bot: System update: latency p95 back to 480ms (12m after mitigation). Monitoring for recurrence.

cust-success-marta: Drafting customer-facing note. Suggest: "We detected elevated latency affecting your traffic this morning. We isolated your workload to a reserved pool and applied mitigations; performance is restored. We will follow up with root cause and a timeline for any credits if SLA affected." Thoughts?

cto-eli: Please quantify customer impact (total affected minutes/hours, % of requests above SLA) so we can include in exec summary. I want a 1-2 slide brief for leadership.

eng-runtime-chandra: Preliminary numbers: ~52 minutes of elevated p95 above SLA threshold, affecting ~11% of PegasusCorp requests in that window. Full log export and trace links: https://logs.redwood/1934567899/export

cust-success-marta: Thanks. For credits: propose an interim offer of "pro-rated service credit for the affected interval" and indicate we'll confirm final credit after RCA. Suggest language: "We will evaluate SLA impact and propose appropriate service credit; an interim goodwill credit of one day of service offered upon request."

cto-eli: Fine as interim. Make sure legal is ok with wording before final.

oncall-sylvia: Action items: 1) eng-runtime to draft RCA outline (owner: chandra) due EOD +1. 2) cust-success to prepare customer email + exec summary (owner: marta) due EOD. 3) infra to propose persistent routing safeguards (owner: jake) due +3 days. I'll file follow-up ticket RN-1934567899.

eng-runtime-chandra: RCA outline (short): - timeline of events - culprit: tenant-induced shard hotspot + routing weight skew + cold KV windows - mitigations applied (isolation, cache window bump) - short-term fixes (routing weight caps, auto-eviction safeguards) - long-term: hot-shard detector + tenant throttling policy. Will attach logs and perf diffs.

cust-success-marta: I'll send the initial customer note now (copying dev/ops). Will coordinate exec brief once chandra posts numbers.

oncall-sylvia: Closing on-call bridge for operational handoff. Will keep this thread as the customer comms + RCA workspace. If latency recurs, re-pager. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
